plan.title: bug(scope): scope:complete has no path for a delivered PR-only brief, and the identity join accepts a post-merge closing link

narratives.Description: scope:complete refuses a code-bearing brief that has a stamped productPullRequest but no github-issue reference, so shipped PR-only work cannot complete honestly. On the issue-anchored path the identity join checks the PR's current closingIssuesReferences, so a closing link added after merge satisfies it, while a Path B product PR that carries only a deft-story mark cannot complete. This story ships a PR-only completion path, an early preflight warning, association proven at merge time, and a refusal of non-delivery dispositions for a merged stamped PR.
narratives.Overview:
- relieves: P1 — Recut13-PR-only-tuple: when resolvePlanGithubIssueRef is null, delivery identity is (repository, prNumber) from plan.metadata.productPullRequest plus the canonically resolved project remote; require --pr equals that number, PR merged, merge_commit_sha equals --merge-commit; --repo matching assertion only; no invented issue closer on this path; the PR-only path has no merge-time association standard in v1.
- relieves: P1 — Recut13-discovery-same-resolver: discoverDeliveryEvidenceForComplete uses that same PR-only derivation when productPullRequest is stamped and issue ref is null (keep delivery-base / ancestry).
- relieves: P1 — Recut13-github-pr-stamp-match-only: x-xbrief/github-pr is not a standalone delivery-identity mark in v1; when productPullRequest is stamped, a matching same-repo URI is redundant and a different historical PR ref does not override or invalidate the stamp; when productPullRequest is unset, do not admit github-pr as delivery identity — remediate by stamping productPullRequest (issue-less briefs only) or adding an issue origin; "resolvePlanGithubIssueRef is null" means today's resolver (first reference whose URI parses as a GitHub issue URL regardless of type).
- relieves: P2 — Recut13-preflight-warn: at xbrief:preflight for isCodeBearingScope without issue origin, print one remediation naming the PR-only complete contract and the issue-first path; promote/activate stay green; warn population is isCodeBearingScope-true briefs.
- relieves: P3 — Recut13-merge-time-association: on the issue-anchored path, the (repository, issue, PR) association is effective at merge when one of these holds: (a) the candidate PR is not delivery-brief-land-excluded, its body as of authoritative merged_at carries a sole deft-story: N mark naming that issue in the same repository (sole = exactly one distinct mark per parseAllDeftStoryMarks), AND at verification time no other merged PR in that repository is an established competitor — a competitor is a merged PR that is not delivery-brief-land-excluded and whose body as of its own merged_at carries a sole deft-story: N for that issue; delivery-brief-land-excluded means every changed path (including rename sources and destinations) is under xbrief|vbrief/(proposed|pending|active|completed)/ or is root CHANGELOG.md, with at least one such path for a positive exclusion (CHANGELOG-only and completed-folder renames qualify; empty/deletion-only diffs that only touch those paths are excluded); this delivery exclusion is not identical to activation isBriefLandShapedDiff; a failed changed-file lookup for the candidate or a possible competitor fails closed; uniqueness is observed among merged non-excluded PRs at verification; (b) the PR body as of merged_at contains a GitHub closing keyword (close, closes, closed, fix, fixes, fixed, resolve, resolves, resolved; case-insensitive) naming that issue as #N, owner/repo#N or the issue URL; (c) ConnectedEvent / DisconnectedEvent history reconstructs a connected state at merged_at; the merge-time body is the latest userContentEdits revision with editedAt ≤ merged_at, or the current body when the PR has no edit history; a mark, keyword or Connected link added after merged_at does not count; current-state closingIssuesReferences alone stays insufficient; brief-in-PR-diff identity is unchanged; no silent fallback from a failed issue-anchored check to the PR stamp.
- relieves: P3 — Recut13-uniqueness-scan-fail-closed: limb (a) scan shape is: enumerate all merged PRs via paged list; for each, reconstruct the merge-time body via fully paged userContentEdits (or current body when no edits); run parseAllDeftStoryMarks; only for sole-mark hits, fetch changed files via paged pulls/<N>/files (including rename previous_filename) to classify delivery-brief-land. Default budget: attempt that full enumeration. Budget units and caps: (1) wall-clock 20 minutes from scan start; (2) before each GraphQL page, live graphql.remaining must be ≥ 200 else refuse; (3) REST core remaining ≥ 100 else refuse. Supported envelope: repositories where full enumeration finishes under those caps under ordinary rate limits (guide: ≤ ~10k merged PRs). Above that envelope, or on any incomplete page / timeout / rate-limit / truncated files listing (forge 3000-file cap) / unreadable revision or competitor / exhausted budget before every merged PR is classified, fail closed (unknown/refuse, no completion). Do not use current-body search alone as completeness; do not silently weaken to a recent window; marks removed after merge without reconstructable merge-time body are fail-closed unknowns. Fixtures cover competing non-excluded mark removed after merge, duplicate beyond first page, unreadable competitor, truncated files listing, budget-exhaustion refuse, product PR that passes when only delivery-excluded PRs share the mark (including completed-folder rename), two non-excluded sole-mark PRs that both refuse, delivery-excluded candidate that refuses even alone, and multi-story mark PR that is not sole for any story; a later-merged competing non-excluded sole mark refuses a later complete without rewriting stored completion provenance.
- relieves: P3 — Recut13-stranded-shape-named: an issue-anchored brief whose product PR carried no unique merge-time sole deft-story mark among non-excluded PRs, no closing keyword and no Connected link at merged_at (including the #6147 shape and other Refs-only / mark-less product PRs) stays fail-closed in v1 with a refusal that names the three accepted bases; recovery is the parked identity-migration.
- relieves: P3 — Recut13-stamp-conjunct-demoted: plan.metadata.productPullRequest === --pr is not a delivery-identity proof on the issue-anchored path in v1; it may remain as first-write stamp durability of a successful complete only (footnote); activation/lifecycle exclusion from the uniqueness set lives in Recut13-merge-time-association delivery-brief-land filter, not in this demotion limb.
- relieves: P4 — Recut13-non-delivery-control: scope:complete refuses a non-delivery disposition (cancelled, superseded, experiment_archived, accepted_not_delivered) when plan.metadata.productPullRequest is stamped and that PR is merged in the authoritative repository; resolve that stamped PR before any successful non-delivery early return; if merge state cannot be established (timeout, inaccessible repository, malformed response), fail closed with a retry/repair diagnostic and perform no completion/provenance mutation; a confirmed unmerged stamped PR remains eligible subject to existing disposition checks; merged-to-integration without delivery-ref proof counts as merged for this refuse in v1 (fixture-covered conservative restriction).

narratives.UserStory: As a maintainer completing a shipped scope, I want scope:complete to accept a PR-only brief and to prove issue association as of merge time, so that delivered work records honestly without placeholder issues or post-merge PR body edits.
narratives.ImplementationPlan: Follow the accepted Prefer-A Recut-13 lean on #5710 (comment 6817282070). In packages/core/src/scope/delivery-evidence.ts, derive the PR-only identity tuple from productPullRequest plus the canonical remote when no issue ref exists, and reuse it in discoverDeliveryEvidenceForComplete. On the issue-anchored path, read the merge-time PR body from fully paged userContentEdits and accept a unique sole deft-story mark among PRs that are not delivery-brief-land-excluded, a closing keyword, or a connected state at merged_at, with the bounded exhaustive scan failing closed. Refuse a non-delivery disposition in scope:complete when the stamped PR is merged. Add the preflight warning in packages/runtime/src/vbrief-preflight.ts. Cover each clause with focused vitest cases that inject the forge fetchers, and add a CHANGELOG Unreleased entry.
narratives.Supersession: The contract is the Recut-13 lean (comment 6817282070): the nine plan items. The six Recut-4 clause texts stay in plan.acceptance.clauses only because verify:ac requires every admitted-source identity pinned on master to remain a clause (#5055). Recut-13 supersedes them, and where they differ from the plan items the plan items govern.

Prefer-A is the right direction for honest PR-only delivery, but cannot bind as written: repository authority and the positive merge-time association proof need tightening. No issue-first hard refusal is needed to resolve either gap.

This is source/control-flow verification, not a live reproduction of GitHub's post-merge mutation behavior or an executed test suite.

## F1 — blocks-the-design: bind the repository independently of completion evidence

Evidence: [verifyStoryPrMergeIdentity](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/b35d8ffa8184b4dbb0f4f5d643e540517c0e67c0/packages/core/src/scope/delivery-evidence.ts#L539) currently derives expected repository from the plan and rejects an evidence-repository mismatch before fetching the PR. productPullRequestFromPlan in orphan-active/running-briefs.ts yields only a number. Draft item 1 instead permits repository from evidence/--repo or the default remote.

Failure: PR numbers are repository-local. For a numeric anchor N, caller-selected --repo can substitute another repository's merged PR N. Merge-SHA equality checks the substituted PR against the supplied SHA; it does not establish the intended repository. Delivery ancestry is a separate constraint and does not make repository identity unique (for example, forks can share commits).

Consequence: bind an expected (repository, PR number) tuple independently of the completion claim. A qualified github-pr reference can supply both; a numeric productPullRequest can use a canonically resolved project repository. Make --repo a matching assertion, not a competing authority. Define conflict behavior when both anchor forms exist; reject disagreement instead of silently picking one. Preserve issue-anchored validation when an issue origin exists. This is the identity/swarm boundary: identical PR numbers across repositories or worktrees must not select another unit's evidence.

## F2 — blocks-the-design: absence of a late edit is not proof of association at merge

Evidence: [ClosingIssueRef and fetch contract](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/b35d8ffa8184b4dbb0f4f5d643e540517c0e67c0/packages/core/src/scope/delivery-evidence.ts#L149) carry repository and issue number only; the query at line 442 returns no association history. The verifier at lines 603–629 checks current membership. Pin searches found no ConnectedEvent/DisconnectedEvent or timelineItems implementation of the proposed historical proof.

Failure: draft item 3 says to reject membership whose connecting event or body edit postdates merged_at. A negative test alone leaves missing/unavailable history unspecified. Conversely, rejecting any later body edit rejects a legitimate pre-merge closer followed by a typo correction. An arbitrary earlier cross-reference, or a link added then removed before merge and restored afterward, is also not sufficient evidence that a closing association was effective at merge.

Consequence: require positive, repository-qualified evidence that this PR's closing association to this issue was effective at the authoritative merge time. Specify the supported evidence source and fail-closed result/remediation for unavailable, incomplete, or ambiguous history. Verify that the chosen forge surface actually exposes the required semantics before binding P3 relief. Test late introduction, valid pre-merge association with harmless later edit, removal/readdition, and missing history. Do not use caller --merged-at or mutable current body as historical authority.

Merge-time closing association is sufficient for the narrow P3 defect when it is actually proved; it is not proof of implementation correctness or immutable original brief intent. No general forge-history framework or ancestry redesign is requested here. The minimum evidence contract needed by item 3 cannot be parked with broader API design.

## F3 — sharpens-framing: cover discovery and choose one concrete early disclosure point

Evidence: [discoverDeliveryEvidenceForComplete](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/b35d8ffa8184b4dbb0f4f5d643e540517c0e67c0/packages/core/src/scope/delivery-evidence.ts#L1646) skips discovery when explicit selectors exist, but at lines 1711–1724 rejects a stamped productPullRequest without an issue-derived repository. scope/main.ts advertises automatic discovery when selectors are omitted. preflight/evaluate.ts's lifecycle-ready evaluation and swarm/readiness.ts's validateCandidate have no delivery-anchor warning; the shared delivery helpers are completion consumers, not an early issue-origin requirement.

Failure: changing only verifyStoryPrMergeIdentity leaves the normal no-selector completion command failing for the same PR-only brief. Also, the draft's 'promote/activate or preflight' leaves P2's actual observable surface undecided.

Consequence: use the same anchor resolver in discovery and explicit verification, retaining existing delivery-branch/ancestry checks. Bind one named early warning point and its message/test, rather than adding gates everywhere. Explain that an anchor must be recorded by completion; a PR need not already exist at promotion. Preserve green early transitions for intentional PR-only work. A test of both explicit and selector-free completion prevents a partial P1 fix.

## F4 — footnote: confirmed baseline, honest dispositions, and envelope mismatch

At the pin, isCodeBearingScope reaches true for non-empty swarm.file_scope unless an earlier explicit non-code override applies. verifyStoryPrMergeIdentity immediately rejects a null issue reference; productPullRequest does not rescue it. The existing stored-provenance guard also uses the code-bearing classifier; it does not supply early completion-contract disclosure.

NON_DELIVERY_DISPOSITIONS really bypass delivery validation, but stamp the selected non-delivery disposition and handoffState implemented. That is not an honest delivered result. The existing remediation already says not to use --non-delivery for shipped work; P4 needs the working delivered path, not another escape enum.

The open-critique envelope/Stop 1 also includes a named refutation-target, contrary to the contract's open-charter envelope rule. I treated it as a claim to verify, not a restriction on the critique. Panel deposit matches the ceiling; sibling completeness is not observable by this critic.

## Pain coverage and strongest rejected readings

P1 is real at the pin. Prefer-A can relieve it with a qualified PR anchor plus both completion entry paths. P2 is real as a missing early disclosure, and a warning is appropriate; no issue-first gate is required. P3 remains unproved by the draft's negative timestamp sketch until F2 is resolved. P4 is relieved by honest delivered completion, not by relabeling shipped work.

Early hard-refuse is strongest when issue-first is an intentional project policy: it is simple and prevents future late surprises. It still strands already-merged PR-only briefs and contradicts the stated intentional PR-only requirement. An explicit operator change to that requirement plus an honest legacy-completion route would change my verdict.

Treating #3583 as solved is strongest because a stamped product PR already drives discovery and reuses the delivery gate. The null-issue branch before its fetch and the downstream identity join refute that reading at this SHA. A pin where both branches accept a qualified PR-only anchor would reverse it.

The non-delivery escape is strongest for genuinely abandoned, superseded, or unshipped work; it is already auditable and avoids forging merge proof. Evidence that this particular work did not ship would make that path correct. It does not solve the delivered case.

### Why

That includes the current through-merge cohort (#5710, #5882, #6203). The batched `swarm:finalize-cohort` would refuse them all.

Keyword closers are also rare on product PRs here. While the brief is in `active/`, `pr:check-closing-keywords` (intent mode, #3015) refuses a real `Closes #N` unless `--allow-close` is passed. So product PRs carry `Tracking: #N` / `Refs #N` plus the `deft-story: N` mark (#4864 / #5782), which the framework already treats as the full-story bind. Merge-time association therefore has to accept that mark too.

GitHub keeps the full PR body for each revision: GraphQL `userContentEdits` returns `diff` (the revision's full text) and `editedAt`. On #6203, two revisions came back, and the latest revision's length equals the current body's length. So the body as of `merged_at` can be read directly. ## In plain English

The reminted P3 clause is mechanically implementable — I re-ran the GraphQL revision probe and the merge-time body really can be read the way the clause assumes. But the clause's warrant is a count taken from *current* PR bodies, and when I retake that count at merge time it collapses: six of the eight PRs the recut cites as keyword closers did not carry the keyword when they merged. What actually rescues the through-merge cohort is the `deft-story` limb — and that limb is many-to-one. Three different merged PRs each carry a sole `deft-story: 6173` at merge time. So the join proves "a PR that mentioned this story", not "the PR that delivered it". One cited PR (#6147) clears neither limb at merge time, so the clause also strands work it was cut to unblock. P1, P2 and P4 relief reads honest; P3 does not, as written.

## Method

Pin-read `git show 75a538684f97c9c4a19d43e7a18b375657af9073:` for `packages/core/src/scope/delivery-evidence.ts`, `orphan-active/running-briefs.ts`, `pr-closing-keywords/main.ts`, `intent-constraint/plan-id-adopter.ts`, `runtime/src/dispatch.ts`, `content/contracts/design-critique.md`. The P3 limb is a claim about forge behaviour, so I also re-ran the recut's own probe read-only via `gh api graphql` over the last 40 merged PRs, reading `userContentEdits{editedAt diff}` and selecting the newest revision with `editedAt <= mergedAt`. No writes, no dest mutation.

## Verified sound (recording what holds)

The revision model the clause depends on checks out. Across all 20 edited PRs in that window, the oldest `userContentEdits` node's `editedAt` equals the PR's `createdAt`, and the newest node's `diff` length equals the current body length. So `diff` is the full body *as of* that revision, and creation is itself recorded as the earliest revision. Two consequences the clause gets right: "latest revision with `editedAt <= merged_at`" is always defined whenever edit history is non-empty, and "current body when the PR has no edit history" is correct because never-edited implies current equals creation. The connection also returned newest-first under both `first:` and `last:`, which is what makes the "fail closed when not fully paged" limb load-bearing rather than decorative.

## Findings

### 1. `blocks-the-design` — the remint's warrant is measured by the method the remint forbids

Evidence. I re-read all eight PRs the recut names (#6146, #6147, #6149, #6150, #6151, #6171, #6176, #6196) at their merge-time revision. Six carry no closing keyword at `merged_at`; the keyword was added afterwards. #6176 merge-time body says `Refs #6173`; the current body says `Closes #6173`, added in a revision at `2026-11-10T21:03:03Z` against `mergedAt 2026-11-10T20:38:47Z`. #6149 gains `Fixes #5916` at `2026-11-09T22:33:42Z` against `mergedAt 2026-11-09T20:10:15Z`. Same shape on #6146, #6147, #6150, #6151. Over the whole 40-PR window, exactly three PRs carry a merge-time keyword closer: #6158 (#6157), #6171 (#4966), #6196 (#5853).

Failure mode. The "Why" reasons from 8-of-40 to the conclusion that keyword closers are a real basis worth admitting. Under this clause's own rule — "a keyword added after `merged_at` does not count" — the merge-time rate is 3-of-40. The stated reason for the remint does not survive its own standard, and the cohort the remint exists to unblock is not in fact carried by the keyword limb.

Disposition consequence. The keyword limb is near-vacuous here, so the whole clause's strength is the `deft-story` limb's strength alone. That has to be stated before anything binds, because finding 2 is then the entire safety case.

### 2. `blocks-the-design` — "sole `deft-story: N`" is many-to-one, so the join stops proving delivery

Evidence. Grouping merge-time bodies in the same window by stories that have more than one PR carrying a *sole* `deft-story` mark: #4966 is sole-marked by #6168, #6169 and #6171; #6173 by #6176, #6177 and #6178; #6136 by #6156 and #6158; #5102 by #6186 and #6190. The `sole` qualifier bounds marks-per-PR, not PRs-per-story. The one-to-one property is an authoring instruction only — `intent-constraint/plan-id-adopter.ts:20` at the dispatch SHA reads "only use the mark on the PR that is the delivery for #N". Nothing enforces it, and the data shows it is not held.

Failure mode. `scope:complete --pr 6177 --merge-commit <6177 merge sha>` satisfies merge-time association for #6173 and stamps `completionProvenance` naming #6177 as the delivery, while #6176 and #6178 are equally eligible. Whichever is passed first wins, silently. `swarm:finalize-cohort` batches this, so the wrong-PR stamp lands unattended. Separately #6158 carries a merge-time keyword closing #6157 *and* a sole `deft-story: 6136`, so one PR satisfies association for two different issues.

Disposition consequence. P3 asks for proof of association-at-merge. This limb proves *mention*-at-merge. The cite as written is not honest relief, and the contract's prohibition applies directly: a safety case that ends at "authors only mark the delivery PR" needs a deterministic control.

Control already in the tree. Conjoin the brief-side bind that is already the documented meaning of the mark: merge-time `deft-story: N` **and** `plan.metadata.productPullRequest === --pr`. That predicate already exists at `pr-closing-keywords/main.ts:311`, and it excludes activation PRs for free because activation requires the stamp unset (`pr-closing-keywords/main.ts:482`). It is a one-conjunct change, not a second mechanism.

### 3. `blocks-the-design` — a cited PR clears neither limb, so the clause strands part of its own cohort

Evidence. #6147's merge-time revision (`2026-11-09T19:43:22Z`, `mergedAt 2026-11-09T20:02:04Z`) carries `Tracking: #5997` and `Related: #5998` — no closing keyword and no `deft-story` mark at all. `Fixes #5997` and `Fixes #5998` appear only in a `2026-11-09T22:34:52Z` revision.

Failure mode. For an issue-anchored brief in that shape, limb (a) fails on both alternatives, limb (b) fails because the recut states none of these issues has a ConnectedEvent, brief-in-PR-diff cannot rescue a Path-B product PR, and the clause forbids silent fallback to the PR stamp while an issue origin remains. Hard refuse with no path.

Disposition consequence. "Tracking plus `deft-story` is what product PRs here carry" is not uniformly true at merge time. Either the parked identity-migration limb is in scope for v1, or the clause should say which merged briefs it knowingly strands. Claiming it unblocks the issue-anchored path overstates it.

### 4. `sharpens-framing` — the PR-only limb reopens P3's forgery on the path P3 does not cover

Evidence. The P1 limb derives identity from `plan.metadata.productPullRequest` plus the resolved remote, with `--repo` as a matching assertion only. That value is a locally written plan field (`orphan-active/running-briefs.ts:150-205`), with no merge-time standard anywhere in the remedy, and the Park list carries "productPullRequest stamp-time freeze vs merged_at as co-equal v1 limb".

Failure mode. Stamp `productPullRequest` after the fact to any merged PR in the repo, pass matching `--pr` and `--merge-commit`, and the join passes — the same post-hoc manufacture P3 names, on the sibling limb.

Disposition consequence. Parking it is honest, so this does not block. But the park line should say plainly that the PR-only path has **no** merge-time association standard in v1, so no reader carries P3's guarantee across to P1.

### 5. `sharpens-framing` — the P1 routing switch is wider than "has a github-issue origin"

Evidence. `delivery-evidence.ts:361-383` at the dispatch SHA: `resolvePlanGithubIssueRef` returns on the first reference whose URI parses as a GitHub issue URL **regardless of its `type`**; the `type.includes("github-issue")` test only gates references whose URI does not parse.

Failure mode. A brief listing a `related` or `see-also` GitHub issue URL ahead of its real origin resolves to the wrong story. An issue-less brief carrying any such URL is routed off the PR-only path onto the issue-anchored path, where the clause's no-silent-fallback rule turns it into a hard refuse whose message names a story the brief never claimed.

Disposition consequence. P1 relief is real but conditional on reference hygiene. The limb's load-bearing phrase "when `resolvePlanGithubIssueRef` is null" should name the typed-and-ordered resolution it assumes, or say that tightening is out of scope.

### 6. `sharpens-framing` — the P4 limb names a prohibition, not a control

Evidence. The limb is "keep `NON_DELIVERY_DISPOSITIONS` honest — no cancelled/superseded/experiment_archived/accepted_not_delivered for shipped PR-only work." No mechanism is named; `NON_DELIVERY_DISPOSITIONS` at `delivery-evidence.ts:55-60` is unchanged.

Failure mode. The escape stays reachable by anyone who prefers it to debugging the gate — which is exactly the pressure P4 was filed about.

Disposition consequence. P4 is relieved *in substance* by P1 (once PR-only completion exists, nothing forces the escape), and on that reading the cite is honest. The limb itself ends at operator attention, which the contract forbids as a closing move. A deterministic control is cheap and local: refuse a non-delivery disposition at `scope:complete` when `productPullRequest` is stamped and that PR is merged.

### 7. `footnote` — the preflight stamp conjunct is inert where it fires, and the probe sampled an issue

`xbrief:preflight` maps to `vbrief-preflight` (`runtime/src/dispatch.ts:470`) and runs before a product PR exists; activation additionally requires the stamp unset (`pr-closing-keywords/main.ts:482`). So "without stamped `productPullRequest`" is always true at that point and discriminates nothing; the limb reduces to "warn every issue-less code-bearing brief at preflight". That behaviour is right — the conjunct is just decoration. Separately, the recut's probe cites "#6203", which is the **issue**, not a pull request; there is no PR #6203, and the product PR #6211 has zero body edits. The property does hold on PRs — I confirmed it on 20 — but the stated evidence did not test the surface the clause reads.

## Verdict

- P1 — honest relief, conditional on finding 5 and with the finding 4 asymmetry left unstated in the park line.
- P2 — honest relief. The pain is "surfaces only after merge"; preflight is before merge, so the pain is met. Leaving promote/activate green is a narrowing the limb states openly, not a silent one.
- P3 — **not honest as written.** The keyword limb is near-vacuous at merge time (1), the `deft-story` limb proves mention rather than delivery and has four real many-to-one instances in a 40-PR window (2), and the disjunction strands at least one PR of the cited cohort outright (3). The clause is well-built machinery pointed at a predicate that does not identify a delivery.
- P4 — relieved in substance via P1; the limb itself names no control (6).

## Road not taken

I considered calling finding 2 `sharpens-framing` on the ground that `deft-story` multiplicity is a data-hygiene problem the framework could fix by enforcing the authoring rule. I did not, because the remedy is being bound *now* against a corpus that already violates the rule, and the clause offers no migration or detection for the existing violations. A proof that depends on a convention the live data breaks is not a proof yet.

## Steelman

The strongest version of the recut: merge-time reading is the real advance, the `deft-story` mark is the framework's own full-story bind, and in practice an operator passes the PR they just merged — so multiplicity is theoretical. What would flip my verdict is either the `productPullRequest === --pr` conjunct from finding 2, which makes multiplicity harmless, or evidence that `swarm:finalize-cohort` already pins the PR independently so `--pr` is never operator-chosen on this path. I looked for the latter at the dispatch SHA and did not find it.

## Injection / swarm lens

It fires: this changes delivery identity and runs under batched cohort finalize. The merge-time body is attacker-controlled text authored by whoever opened the PR, and `deft-story: N` is self-asserted with no forge-side arbitration. Reading the merge-time revision correctly removes the post-merge edit vector, which is the real gain here. It does not remove the at-open vector: a PR opened with a sole `deft-story: N` naming someone else's story is association under this clause from the moment it merges. The `productPullRequest` conjunct closes that too, because the stamp is written brief-side.

## Summary

A brief that is tracked by PR only (no `x-xbrief/github-issue` reference) can be promoted, activated, implemented and merged, and then `scope:complete` refuses it. The only way to record the delivery is to create a new issue after the fact and edit the merged PR's body to say `Closes #<new issue>`. That post-merge edit then satisfies the identity join, which shows the join does not prove what it is meant to prove.

Observed on `@deftai/directive-core` 0.125.0. The logic in `scope/delivery-evidence.js` is unchanged in 0.125.2.

## What happens

1. A consumer brief has no `x-xbrief/github-issue` reference. Its origins are spec sections, a user request and decision records. It carries `plan.metadata.productPullRequest: <n>` and a non-empty `plan.metadata.swarm.file_scope`.
2. Promote, activate, preflight and readiness all pass. None of them requires an issue origin.
3. The product PR merges.
4. `scope:complete -- <active brief> --merge-commit <sha> --pr <n>` fails:
   `Delivery identity join failed: plan has no x-xbrief/github-issue reference to derive expected repository/issue (#3675).`
5. The operator's agent creates a new issue whose body says it exists only to satisfy the identity join. It binds that issue into the brief and edits the already-merged PR's body to add `Closes #<new issue>`. GitHub adds the issue to the merged PR's `closingIssuesReferences`, and completion can proceed.

## Why this is a defect

- **No PR-only completion path.** `isCodeBearingScope` returns true for any brief with a non-empty `swarm.file_scope`, even without an issue reference. `verifyStoryPrMergeIdentity` then derives the expected identity only from `resolvePlanGithubIssueRef(plan)` and hard-fails when it is null. `plan.metadata.productPullRequest` is not consulted. Every `NON_DELIVERY_DISPOSITIONS` value (`cancelled`, `superseded`, `experiment_archived`, `accepted_not_delivered`) would misrecord work that shipped. So a delivered PR-only brief cannot complete honestly.
- **The requirement surfaces only after merge.** `hasGithubIssueRef` / `resolvePlanGithubIssueRef` / `isCodeBearingScope` are used only by `scope/delivery-evidence.js`. Nothing at promote, activate, `xbrief:preflight` or `swarm:readiness` warns that a code-bearing brief will need an issue origin to complete.
- **The identity join can be satisfied retroactively.** The join checks the PR's current `closingIssuesReferences`. GitHub updates that list when a merged PR's body is edited, so a link added after merge passes. The join therefore does not prove the PR was associated with the story when it merged.

## Expected

One of these, plus the third point in either case:

1. For a code-bearing brief with no issue reference, accept `plan.metadata.productPullRequest` (or an `x-xbrief/github-pr` reference) as the identity anchor: require `--pr` to equal it, the PR to be merged, and `merge_commit_sha` to equal `--merge-commit`.
2. Or refuse early: promote/activate (or preflight) fails a code-bearing brief that has no issue origin, with a remediation that names the issue-first path, so the gap is found before implementation rather than after merge.
3. Either way, judge closing-issue association as of merge time (for example, reject a closing link whose connecting event or body edit postdates `merged_at`), so a post-merge edit cannot manufacture identity.

## Actual cost

One placeholder issue created only to satisfy the gate, a post-merge edit to a merged PR body, and an extra bind commit on the active brief before the lifecycle PR could open.

## Related

#3675 (identity join), #3583, #4864, #3791.
